facts.F1: The Applicant was working in the construction of a tunnel from Sheung Shui to Chau Tau in the New Territories under a Kowloon-Canton Railway Corporation project.
facts.F2: On 27 September 2004, the Applicant was instructed to enter an air-compressed chamber of a tunnel-boring machine for cleaning work, where he experienced ear pain due to increasing air compression.
facts.F3: The Applicant claimed to have suffered pain in both ears and loss of hearing in his right ear after the incident.
facts.F4: The Applicant was referred to see the appointed doctor, Dr. Jonathan Wai, and was given 3 days of medications and sick leave.
facts.F5: The Applicant returned to work for 18-19 days in October 2004 but ceased working altogether since 27 October 2004.
facts.F6: The Applicant sought treatment from Yan Chai Hospital and a general practitioner, Dr. Alfred Lo, who issued various sick leave certificates.
facts.F7: The Employees' Compensation (Ordinary Assessment) Board assessed the Applicant to have suffered 0% loss of earning capacity, which was affirmed upon review.
facts.F8: The Applicant appealed against the assessment, while the Respondent also lodged an appeal against the same.
facts.F9: Dr. Ng Tat Yuen and Dr. Simon Wong provided expert evidence on the Applicant's hearing ability.
facts.F10: Dr. Simon Wong's analysis of the Applicant's hearing ability took into account the results of various PTAs and objective tests.
facts.F11: Dr. Lo did not arrange for the Applicant to undertake any tests on his hearing impairment.
facts.F12: Dr. Lo issued sick leave certificates for the Applicant after 30 September 2004, despite lack of medical evidence supporting the Applicant's hearing condition.

facts.F2: On 9 January 2008, Mr. Ka Bahadur was dismantling a platform made of iron beams and steel plates when he slipped on the wet surface of the platform, fell from a height of about 2.5m to the ground.
facts.F3: As a result, Mr. Ka Bahadur suffered injuries to his head and clavicle and had a fracture in the right ribs.
facts.F4: He was admitted to hospital on 9 January 2008 and discharged on 2 February 2008.
facts.F5: On 22 July 2008, Mr. Ka Bahadur filed this Application for compensation to the Court under section 18A of the Ordinance.

facts.F8: The period of sick leave certified as necessary due to the injury was from 9 January 2008 to 2 April 2009.
facts.F9: Mr. Ka Bahadur's loss of earning capacity permanently caused by the injury was certified to be 5%.

facts.F11: On 14 August 2009, judgment on liability was entered against Yuk Tong for damages to be assessed.
facts.F12: No appeal was made against the Board's assessment of loss of earning capacity.

claim: The plaintiff claims for compensation under the Employees' Compensation Ordinance, Cap. 282 (ECO) in respect of an injury by accident happened at the warehouse in Tuen Mun on 12 April 2012.

facts.F1: The applicant claims to have been employed by the respondent at the time of the accident and that the accident occurred while he was transporting bags of leather with another co-worker by stacking the bags on a wooden plank.
facts.F2: The respondent denied the existence of any employment relationship and contended that the applicant was a member of the delivery team to whom the respondent has sub-contracted the services.
facts.F3: There was no written contract between the respondent and the applicant or the delivery team.
facts.F4: The respondent did not challenge the applicant's injury as recorded in the medical reports.
facts.F5: The Employees' Compensation (Ordinary Assessment) Board assessed the applicant to have suffered 15% loss of earning capacity with the sick leave period from 12 April 2012 to 24 November 2014.
facts.F6: The respondent has not adduced any evidence to rebut the assessment.
facts.F7: The applicant was interviewed by Mr Kong Tak Ping (Kong) for the job, who told him that his salary would be calculated on a daily basis with reference to the sales of the respondent.
facts.F8: The applicant took up the job on 16 February 2011.
facts.F9: The respondent assigned the daily schedule and route journeys for the applicant and his colleagues, including the arrangements for destination of delivery and the goods that each of the workers shall deliver.
facts.F10: The respondent calculated the monthly salary of the applicant and paid him the salary in cash.
facts.F11: The applicant has no financial loss, the respondent gave all piers entrance fees to the applicant for their payment, and the respondent was responsible for the payment of penalty tickets received in the course of their works.
facts.F12: All the orders were received by the respondent, who was responsible for recruitment and management.
facts.F13: The applicant did not have any business registration.
facts.F14: The respondent provided the truck and some loading and unloading equipment.
facts.F15: A former colleague of the applicant, Mr Tam Wai Yin, gave evidence that the workers working for the respondent were not independent delivery contractors and that they worked for the respondent and were under the supervision of the respondent.
facts.F16: The applicant's evidence was that the Accident happened on 12 April 2012 while he was transporting bags of leather with another co-worker by stacking the bags on a wooden plank.
facts.F17: The applicant did not realize the seriousness of the injury at that time and he continued to drive the truck to deliver the goods to the Yuan Long warehouse.
facts.F18: When he unloaded the goods at the Yuan Long warehouse, the applicant felt pain at his back and took some rest, and then called the respondent.
facts.F19: Kong asked the applicant to drive the truck back to the car park before he consults the doctor.
facts.F20: The applicant attended the A&E Department of the North District Hospital in the afternoon.
facts.F21: The medical report recorded that the applicant was attended by the doctor at 4:22 pm on 12 April 2012 as a result of industrial accident.
facts.F22: The symptoms were 'back pain after lifting heavy object on the day of attendance'.
facts.F23: The respondent's evidence was that the Accident did not happen, but this was not supported by any documentary evidence.
facts.F24: The court found that the respondent had control over the works of the applicant and other members of the delivery team.
facts.F25: The applicant had no financial risk, and the respondent was responsible for the payment of traffic fines and expenses incurred in the course of delivering goods.
facts.F26: There was no evidence to support the respondent's assertion that the applicant was free to take up orders other than from the respondent.
facts.F27: The respondent did not provide any documentary evidence to support their contention that the Accident did not happen.

facts.F1: Panalpina (Hong Kong) Limited, a wholly owned Hong Kong subsidiary of the Swiss-based air freight company, Panalpina Welt Transport A.G., employed Mr. Ulrich Haldemann as a Chief Accountant in June 1979.
facts.F2: Mr. Haldemann and another expatriate, Mr. Rohrer, were both close friends and worked together at Panalpina Hong Kong.
facts.F3: Both Mr. Haldemann and Mr. Rohrer developed bad habits of chronic lateness to work, especially on Saturdays.
facts.F4: Their tardiness was addressed by their General Manager, Mr. Frischknecht, through memoranda and conversations.
facts.F5: After arriving late on July 17, 1982, Mr. Frischknecht ordered them home, which they perceived as a dismissal.
facts.F6: However, they were told they had not been sacked, and they were asked to report to the office by 10 a.m. the following day.
facts.F7: They did not comply and Mr. Frischknecht sent a letter to them and to the Head Office in Switzerland with a deadline for their return to work or resignation.
facts.F8: Both Mr. Haldemann and Mr. Rohrer failed to meet the deadline or submit a proper letter of resignation, leading to their instant dismissal by Mr. Ruoff from Switzerland.
facts.F9: Mr. Haldemann claimed wrongful dismissal, but the court ruled in favor of Panalpina Hong Kong.
facts.F10: Additionally, Mr. Haldemann rented his flat at Aberdeen Centre to Panalpina Hong Kong through a tenancy agreement, which did not specify a term tied to his employment contract.
facts.F11: After his dismissal, Mr. Haldemann claimed unpaid rent and damages, but the court ruled in favor of Panalpina Hong Kong due to an implied term in the tenancy agreement that it would terminate with the employment contract.
facts.F12: Mr. Frischknecht had the power and authority to set a deadline for Mr. Haldemann's return to work or resignation.
facts.F13: The conversation between Mr. Haldemann and Mr. Frischknecht regarding Mr. Haldemann's return to work was analyzed by the court.
facts.F14: Mr. Haldemann was awarded two months' leave pay and a return flight to Switzerland under his employment contract.
